mission: Ben and Talon return from Tarn Velos under pressure. Luke (off-world at Shedu Maad) is doing what he can from distance to contain contradictory prison reports. Because bringing Talon straight to the Jedi would make the case official before there is anything Saba could act on, Ben takes him to the old Skywalker family apartment on Coruscant as a temporary hideout and supply stop. The apartment exposes more of Ben’s family history than Ben intends: a preserved family holo on a shelf, Luke’s quiet stack of old mission logs left where he placed them years ago, traces of Ben’s own GAG past in things he never threw away. Talon jokes until he realizes the room is not funny. Using the recovered fragment and the apartment’s old secure terminal, Talon identifies Iressa Vossk as the person who can prove where the hidden duplicate manifest went.
why_now: The prison escape has burned every safe location Ben had — he can’t bring Talon to the Jedi without making the case official before there is anything Saba can act on. The apartment is the only place the Vigil doesn’t have an address for either of them, and the old secure terminal there is the only tool left to identify the next lead.
conflict: Ben needs Talon’s expertise to crack the fragment’s next clue, but bringing a convicted prisoner into the family apartment means exposing the wound the room carries. Talon’s jokes probe the room until the family holo stops him — Ben’s silence is more revealing than anything he could say.
turning_point: Talon names Iressa Vossk, and Ben realizes the next lead is not in a battlefield, prison, or Jedi archive — it is inside someone’s carefully rebuilt ordinary life.
closing_hook: Talon names Iressa Vossk, and Ben realizes the next lead is not in a battlefield, prison, or Jedi archive — it is inside someone’s carefully rebuilt ordinary life.
setting: Coruscant, the old Skywalker family apartment — the small residential unit Luke and Mara kept on Coruscant when the Order still had a temple here; the last Skywalker address on the world that later voted the Order out. The vacated Jedi Temple is a few kilometers off, invisible from this apartment but present in the way of something you have memorized the absence of. Climate-control set to whatever it was on Luke's last visit. A preserved family holo on a shelf (Mara, Luke, young Ben). A quiet stack of Luke's old mission logs left on a side table — the work he set down when they relocated to Shedu Maad and never came back to collect. A copy of the Jade Shadow's maintenance registry tucked between the logs: Mara's ship, in Mara's handwriting, the last practical trace of her that was never thrown away. The kitchen still has a few of Mara's training-snack tins. The room reads as wounded but unforgotten.
emotional_trajectory: Make the apartment a human breather, not a nostalgia shrine. Ben should be competent and defensive, embarrassed by intimacy more than danger. Talon should puncture solemnity until he accidentally touches something real (the holo, specifically — he makes a small dark joke, sees Ben’s face, stops). This is Talon’s first time in the apartment. The reader should feel the threshold-crossing — Ben bringing a near-stranger into his family’s private space — without it being underlined.

stakes.personal: Ben has spent years categorizing the GAG year away. Talon’s presence in the apartment — where Mara’s face looks out from a shelf and Luke’s old mission logs are still stacked where he left them — forces Ben to hold the wound and the work in the same room at the same time. Being seen here is more frightening than being shot at.
stakes.interpersonal: Talon’s first instinct is to joke everything flat — but when he reads the family holo and makes a small dark quip, Ben’s face closes. That instant of stopped silence is the first moment Talon treats Ben as a person rather than a job. Neither of them will name it.
stakes.external: Luke is containing contradictory prison reports from Shedu Maad. Every hour they waste without the next lead is another hour Greyline has to clean up or accelerate. The name Iressa Vossk has to come out of the terminal tonight.

sensory_details: The apartment's recycled air smells of old climate-control and Mara's training-snack tins, a particular dry sweetness that has no business surviving this many years. The family holo on the shelf casts its own small glow — Mara's face, Luke's hand on young Ben's shoulder — static and present. Tucked between Luke's mission logs on the side table, the Jade Shadow's maintenance registry in Mara's handwriting: columns of service dates and part numbers, her shorthand in the margins. Talon's eyes move to it once and Ben does not explain it. The rain on the transparisteel is the only moving thing in the room until Talon starts filling the silence.
canon_elements_needed: Shedu Maad / Hapes Jedi HQ continuity
Tarn Velos prison geography and legal stakes
Skywalker apartment as last Skywalker presence on the world that exiled the Order
Mara Jade Skywalker — her history in the apartment; the Jade Shadow maintenance registry as a named family trace
Luke's mission logs as the work set down when the Order left Coruscant — unforgotten, uncollected
Vacated Jedi Temple: present in the city but not visible from this apartment; absence as a felt fact, not a view

turning_point_detail.trigger: Talon runs the fragment's audit signature against his own memory of the old transfer chain and names Iressa Vossk — not as a guess but as the only analyst he ever knew who could prove a cloned identity from surrounding records damage.
turning_point_detail.shift: Ben realizes the next lead isn't in a battlefield or archive. It's inside someone's carefully rebuilt ordinary life — and reaching her means disturbing it.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben has now brought a convicted prisoner into the family apartment and shared the secure terminal. If anything goes wrong from here, there is no version of this that looks like the right call.

emotional_arc.start: Controlled and competent — Ben is managing the practical crisis (hiding Talon, accessing the terminal) and suppressing the emotional weight of being back in the apartment.
emotional_arc.shift: Talon's accidental probe of the family holo — the dark joke, the stopped look — cracks Ben's professional surface. For a moment, Talon sees more than Ben intended to show.
emotional_arc.end: Ben refocuses on the work. The wound is covered. But something has shifted in the room: Talon is no longer just cargo, and Ben can feel that he has shown something he can't take back.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben routes them to the family apartment as the only location Vigil records don't carry, and the room's preserved objects immediately expose more of his history than he planned.
key_beats.state_change: Talon moves from passenger to witness — he is now inside Ben's private wound, not just alongside the mission.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The instinct to explain something — the holo, the logs — fires and is swallowed; covering with movement to the terminal instead.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon fills the silence with jokes; Mara's training-snack tins and the recycled air make the apartment feel inhabited by something that doesn't answer back.
key_beats.state_change: The room's weight accumulates under Talon's jokes rather than being dispersed by them — the jokes are measuring something, not deflecting it.
key_beats.pov_reaction: A low irritation that isn't really irritation — closer to the feeling of a door being tried.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon makes a small dark joke about the family holo, reads Ben's face, and stops.
key_beats.state_change: The dynamic shifts: Talon stops performing and the room goes genuinely quiet for the first time.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The face closing happens before the decision to close it — then the effort to keep working, hands finding the terminal.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Talon work the secure terminal together; Talon runs the recovered fragment against the transfer-chain pattern he carries from his own conviction record.
key_beats.state_change: The investigation moves from reconnaissance to active identification — the fragment is no longer just evidence, it's a key.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Leaning into the work with relief — the terminal is ground that doesn't shift under him.

key_beats.beat_description: Talon names Iressa Vossk as the only analyst who could prove a cloned shipment identity from the damage pattern around the missing records.
key_beats.state_change: The next lead resolves: it is not in an archive or a prison but inside someone's carefully rebuilt ordinary life.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The recognition landing as something heavier than useful — the pull toward what that costs her, held back.

notes:
Source: Chapter Outlines v4.1. Act: Act Two — Coruscant Investigation / Foundation / The Vigil. Chapter title: Back Through the Rain.

Reader-onboarding note: Use physical objects, but only two primary: the family holo (Mara, Luke, young Ben — the photo Luke kept) and Luke’s stack of old mission logs (the work he set down years ago and never returned to). The Jade Shadow registry is a third, lighter object — one glance from Talon, no commentary. All three are texture, not Chekhov’s gun. The reader should understand that Ben’s family loves him, but the apartment holds wounds no one has fully sorted. Avoid stacking too many objects — the room should breathe.

Texture thread: The Jade Shadow registry is Mara’s last practical handwriting in the apartment — ship maintenance, not sentiment. The drafter should let it be what it is: a working document Mara kept for a ship that no longer needs it.

Continuity note: This is the first time Talon sees the apartment. Ben and Talon will return here later (post-PP2) under very different circumstances. The drafter should write this visit as a one-night brush past the wound, so that the eventual return reads as a return.

Character voice focus: preserve the exact v1.4 character behavior and dialogue rules for the chapter POV and named participants. Plot first, character second, theme through consequences.
